title: Choosing Data Stores, Caching and Data Lifecycles

header.html: Manage data lifecycles with S3 Lifecycle policies, TTL and retention periods (1.3.1); choose AWS data stores based on access patterns (1.3.2); determine the appropriate caching solution based on data store selection (1.3.3)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 1.3

html:
1Choosing a data store

Access pattern Best fit
Files, images, backups, static content Amazon S3 (object storage)
Key-value or document lookups at scale, millisecond latency Amazon DynamoDB
Relational data, joins, transactions, SQL Amazon RDS or Amazon Aurora
Very fast reads of hot data, session data Amazon ElastiCache (in-memory)
Search and log analytics Amazon OpenSearch Service
Block storage for one EC2 instance Amazon EBS
Shared file system across instances Amazon EFS

Exam tip

. Decide by the access pattern first: lookup by key, SQL joins, large objects, or microsecond caching.

2Caching

Service Caches Notes
Amazon ElastiCache (Redis, Memcached) Any query result or session Redis: data structures, persistence, replication; Memcached: simple, multi-threaded
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) DynamoDB reads Drop-in for DynamoDB, no code changes beyond the client; microsecond reads
Amazon CloudFront Web and API content at the edge Reduces latency and origin load
API Gateway cache API responses per stage TTL based

Caching strategies

Strategy How it works Trade-off
Lazy loading (cache-aside) Read the cache; on a miss, read the database and fill the cache Only requested data cached; stale data possible
Write-through Write the database and the cache together Cache stays current; writes cost more, cache may hold unused data
TTL Each entry expires after a time Limits staleness
Exam tip

. Relational database overloaded by repeated reads = ElastiCache. DynamoDB reads need microseconds with no rewrite = DAX.

3Data lifecycles

Tool What it does
S3 Lifecycle policies Transition objects to cheaper storage classes (for example, Standard to Standard-IA to Glacier) and expire (delete) them after a time
S3 versioning Keep previous versions; lifecycle rules can expire old versions
DynamoDB TTL A timestamp attribute marks when an item expires; DynamoDB deletes it for free in the background
Retention periods SQS message retention, CloudWatch Logs retention, backup retention
Exam tip

. A cache cannot fix a bad access pattern: pick the store by how data is read, then add a cache for repeated reads.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An application stores user profile images of varying sizes. Which store fits?

  • AAmazon RDS
  • BAmazon ElastiCache
  • CAmazon EBS only
  • DAmazon S3
Show the answer

Answer: D. S3 is object storage for files and images.

S2A relational database is slow because the same queries repeat constantly. What should the developer add?

  • AAmazon ElastiCache in front of the database
  • BA larger S3 bucket so that the database queries can be stored as objects
  • CA dead-letter queue for the queries that the database cannot answer
  • DA second Lambda function that repeats the same queries in parallel
Show the answer

Answer: A. A cache absorbs repeated reads.

S3A DynamoDB-based API needs microsecond read latency with minimal code change. What fits?

  • ADAX
  • BElastiCache for Memcached with custom code
  • CCloudFront only
  • DA larger table
Show the answer

Answer: A. DAX is a DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache.

S4Log files must move to cheaper storage after 30 days and be deleted after a year. Which feature handles this?

  • AAn S3 Lifecycle policy
  • BDynamoDB TTL
  • CSQS retention
  • DCloudFront invalidation
Show the answer

Answer: A. Lifecycle rules transition and expire objects.

S5Session items in DynamoDB should disappear automatically after expiry. What should the developer use?

  • AA scan job that deletes the expired items every hour
  • BA global secondary index on the session timestamp attribute
  • CA conditional write that overwrites the old session on each login
  • DTTL on a timestamp attribute
Show the answer

Answer: D. TTL deletes expired items automatically.

S6A cache is filled only when data is requested and a miss reads the database. Which strategy is this?

  • AWrite-through
  • BReplication
  • CSharding
  • DLazy loading
Show the answer

Answer: D. That is lazy loading (cache-aside).

4.2 Recall questions

R1Which store suits relational data with joins?

Show the answer

Amazon RDS or Aurora.

R2What does DAX cache?

Show the answer

DynamoDB reads.

R3What is write-through caching?

Show the answer

Writing the database and the cache together.

R4What does an S3 Lifecycle policy do?

Show the answer

Transitions objects to other storage classes and expires them.

R5What does DynamoDB TTL do?

Show the answer

Deletes items automatically after a timestamp.

R6Name the two ElastiCache engines.

Show the answer

Redis and Memcached.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Stores S3 objects, DynamoDB key-value, RDS/Aurora SQL, ElastiCache memory
Cache ElastiCache (any), DAX (DynamoDB), CloudFront (edge), API Gateway cache
Strategies lazy loading, write-through, TTL
Lifecycle S3 Lifecycle, DynamoDB TTL, retention settings
